bullets.title: NVDA: CEO scandal, export control risk, PT cuts — but Q3 beat still expected Nov 17
bullets.body: Citi trimmed NVDA PT 10% to $285 (19x CY27E P/E, maintains Buy) citing CEO Jensen Huang investigation into alleged ties with Chinese intelligence asset Alice Huang and $7.5B+ chip shipments to China; White House considering tighter export controls. Separately, one analyst values NVDA 25-30% lower in a Huang-removal scenario (15% probability). Despite the overhang, Q3 beat-and-raise is widely expected Nov 17, and Asia press reports of order cuts were dismissed as inconsistent with supply-chain checks. BofA removed NVDA from its US 1 List.

bullets.title: NET: Strong Q3 beat/raise; tier-1 AI platform narrative intact; PT range $190–$400
bullets.body: Cloudflare Q3 revenue $782.5M beat 6.2%, billings beat 7.8%, EPS $0.38 beat 11.8%; Q4 guided $845-846M (+6.2%). Workers platform and Act IV agent traffic monetization cited as drivers. Sell-side 75% Buy; RBC lowered PT to $350 (from $405) on peer valuation derating but maintains Outperform; Wells Fargo Overweight at $400. DZ Bank upgraded to Buy with $300 target. Guggenheim outlier Sell at $190 DCF-based.

bullets.title: TTD: Big Q3 beat driven by political spend, but durability questioned; DA Davidson downgrades to Neutral
bullets.body: TTD Q3 revenue $736M vs consensus $651M, adj. EBITDA margins 36.1% vs 25% consensus; stock +35% then pulling back. DA Davidson downgrades to Neutral citing political spend as one-time and less durable. Citi maintains Sell/High Risk, raising PT modestly to $12 from $11. Pre-market TTD -7% after +20% after-hours; Q4 guidance at least $755M above FactSet.

bullets.title: TTWO: GTA VI pre-orders 'unprecedented'; street 94% Buy, $290 PT; Nov 19 launch is key catalyst
bullets.body: TTWO Q2 EPS beat by $0.03 but net bookings missed 1.2%; FY27 guidance reaffirmed conservatively (EPS -15.4%, bookings -6%). GTA VI launches Nov 19 with pre-orders described as 'far above' initial expectations; BMO estimates 55M units at $59 ASP. Street consensus 94% Buy, avg PT $290.17 (40% upside); NTM P/E 23.6x vs 5-yr avg 29x, viewed as attractive entry. MS and GS both rate Buy.

bullets.title: AXON: MS maintains OW/$485 PT; post-earnings caution seen as overdone at 0.2x EV/sales/growth
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley keeps Overweight on AXON at $485 PT after Q3 earnings sparked investor concern over core growth, Dedrone margin drag, and 2027 guidance reset risk. Street moved FY27/28 revenue growth to ~27% from ~30%, FCF estimates down ~21% to $594M. AXON trades at 0.2x EV/28E Sales/Growth vs ~0.5x software peer average — MS argues discount more than prices in reset risk. Body Camera 5 spring launch initiates ~3-year refresh cycle.

bullets.title: GEV: PORTS Pike project (8% of backlog) faces financing risk; data-center durability concerns weigh
bullets.body: GEV's PORTS Pike project represents ~8% of Power & Electrification backlog through early 2030s; new investors needed to fund it or GEV reallocates slots (retains deposits). Uncertainty signals broader market concern about US data-center buildout durability and equipment price erosion risk. Rising rates from hot CPI add an additional headwind for the group.

bullets.title: COHR/LITE: Down 5-8% pre-market as Microsoft lobbies Trump to abandon Chinese optical transceiver ban
bullets.body: Microsoft is pushing the Trump administration to abandon a planned ban on Chinese optical transceivers, directly pressuring COHR and LITE in pre-market. Broader semis weak: MRVL -4.6%, VRT -4.8%.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO: $70-78/share, $1.18-1.32T valuation; NVDA, AMD, AVGO, GOOGL, MSFT, MU, TSMC in $26B concurrent placement
bullets.body: Anthropic launching 825M-share IPO at $70-78 (97% primary), implying ~$61B raise with $26B concurrent private placement from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC. Valuation $1.18-1.32T pre-money (down from $1.5-2T prior expectations), 8.1-9.1x 2027E EV/revenue. Pricing expected Nov 18, trading Nov 19-20. Annualized revenue run rate $81B as of Oct 31.

bullets.title: DKNG: Double downgrade — Berenberg and Wells Fargo cut to Hold/EW; PTs $20-21
bullets.body: DraftKings downgraded to Hold by Berenberg (PT $20 from $27.50) and to Equal Weight by Wells Fargo (PT $21 from $30) on regulatory uncertainty and the magnitude of a recent EBITDA guidance cut.

bullets.title: META: Enterprise AI sales build-out + IMAX VR + Ember model launch
bullets.body: META is building an enterprise AI sales operation to monetize AI investment via SMB and consulting partnerships. VR Glasses will be the first IMAX Enhanced certified VR device (immersive app spring 2027). Separately, META unveiled Ember AI model matching competitors' token costs at a fraction of the cost. META declined -1% despite broader internet sector strength.

bullets.title: ADBE/GOOGL: Deepen AI partnership — Gemini in Acrobat/Creative Suite, Firefly in Google Search
bullets.body: Adobe and Google expanded their AI partnership: Acrobat integrates into Google Workspace (Drive/Gmail), Gemini powers Acrobat AI, Firefly/Photoshop/Premiere/Express integrate Google imaging/video models, and Adobe creative tools come to AI Mode in Google Search. Adobe also suspended from PERM H-1B program per VP Vance.

bullets.title: AMZN/GOOGL: Internet sector outperformed; hyperscaler FCF strain and capex crowding out buybacks
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes AMZN +8% and GOOGL +2% led the internet sector (up 4% vs SPX/NDX -3/-5%), trading at 20x and 15x forward 2026 EPS. However, quant analysis flags hyperscaler financial strain: AMZN and GOOGL show sharp FCF declines and rising debt as capex hits 41% of S&P 500 cash use — first quarter since 2021 where capex exceeded total shareholder returns.

bullets.title: APP: US ecommerce stores accelerating; +71% recent move flagged
bullets.body: Citi notes APP US ecommerce stores accelerating to 3.0% w/w growth in Q4 QTD vs 1.5% avg in Q3. APP surged +71% per MS internet sector note.

bullets.title: WIX: -11% on weaker FCF guidance; BofA downgrades to Underperform, cuts PT to $68
bullets.body: WIX fell 11% after reporting weaker FCF guidance despite better Q3 revenue/bookings; Partners revenue slowed to +11% y/y from +17%. Base44 nearing $250M ARR with 58% gross margin but accelerating S&M spend cuts FY26 FCF margin to 16% from high-teens. BofA downgraded to Underperform, cutting PT to $68 from $75.

bullets.title: NBIS: Q3 earnings 11/12; consensus $907M revenue, 38.8% EBITDA margin; options imply ~17% move
bullets.body: Nebius Group reports Q3 on Nov 12; FactSet consensus expects $907M revenue, $351.8M adj. EBITDA (38.8% margin), FY capex $20-25B. Stock up 26.8% since Aug 11, outpacing S&P. EPS beaten 7 of last 8 quarters; last four earnings moves: +34%, +16%, +1%, -7%. Short interest 21%.

bullets.title: CRWV and AI/HPC hosts: Roth survey to assess enterprise GPU hosting demand vs ex-miners
bullets.body: Roth QSG planning a 100-150 decision-maker survey on AI/ML infrastructure procurement, specifically assessing CoreWeave vs converted bitcoin miners (HUT, WULF, CORZ, NBIS) on selection criteria including GPU generation, power, uptime, and solvency.

bullets.title: IBM/ADBE/MSFT: H-1B/PERM crackdowns hitting IT consulting; ACN, CTSH, INFY move to lows
bullets.body: IBM ending visa and green card sponsorship for Consulting division employees. VP Vance suspended Microsoft's access to PERM program over alleged H-1B abuse; Labor Secretary suspended Adobe from PERM. IT consulting stocks ACN, CTSH, INFY moved to lows following White House press conference on H-1B restrictions.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure flow: heavy selling, near-zero dip-buying; semis down 30% from June peak
bullets.body: Oppenheimer sales desk reports heavy selling in AI infrastructure with almost zero dip-buying; sell-to-buy ratio last week approximately 2-3:1. MS notes SOX forward P/E fell from 26.3x (June) to 13.4x, matching historical downturn median. One analyst sees SOX needing a retest of the April breakout (8,000-8,300), implying 12-15% additional downside before a durable advance.

bullets.title: Hot October CPI: core +0.3% m/m; 50bp Dec hike on table; rates headwind for tech
bullets.body: October core CPI printed 0.30% m/m (consensus 0.22%), supercore 0.40%; third consecutive hot print with 56% of categories rising >3% YoY. Fed Governor Waller signaled openness to 50bp December hike if inflation at or above 0.3%. 2Y yield +13bps; core PCE nowcast tracking ~0.33-0.35% for October. Market baseline shifts toward 25bp Dec + 25bp March, with Jan increasingly discussed.

bullets.title: RBLX: Jefferies Underperform/$35 PT; bull/bear debate Nov 16 on 2027 bookings and margin path
bullets.body: Jefferies rates RBLX Underperform with $35 PT; key debate is whether RBLX can return to double-digit bookings growth in 2027 as comps ease and whether late-2026 investments allow margin expansion. Bull/bear panel with James Heaney and Jeff Favuzza set for Nov 16 in NYC.
